newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil mulls options for Heidrun North.
newsitem.headline: Statoil mulls options for Heidrun North.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it was considering three development solutions for the Heidrun North oil find off mid-Norway.
The reservoir could be produced through extended-reach wells from the nearby Heidrun tension leg platform (TLP), Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Alternatively, subsea wells on the field might be tied back to the TLP, or a third option would be a stand-alone development using a production ship, Statoil said.
Preliminary calculations suggested Heidrun North contained about 50 million barrels of oil. An appraisal well may be drilled this year or in 1998 to firm up the estimates, the company said.
Heidrun North was discovered by an exploration well in 1990 and could begin producing in 1999 at the earliest, it said.
